REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - MARCH 10, 2016 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
COUNCIL CHAMBERS, BLOOMFIELD AVENUE AT 183RD STREET
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
MARCH 10, 2016, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Alex Kim, First Evangelical Church of Cerritos.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by representatives from the Long Beach Camp Fire
  Clubs.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair George Ray
  Mayor/Chair Carol Chen

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Proclamations were presented as follows:

  Aaron Chough, Jason Kim, Jonathan Lin, and Brian Shieh (Eagle Scout recipients from
  Troop 72)

  Virginia Loarca, Albert Delapaz, Iana Delapaz, and Eryn Delapaz (Life Saving Rescue)

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Jose Fierro and Miya Walker, representing Cerritos College, spoke regarding the
  “Cerritos Complete” program.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated March 10, 2016
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the Register of
  Demands for the City of Cerritos dated March 10, 2016 in the total amount of
  $7,602,474.42 (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  March 10, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 5

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos
  Redevelopment Agency dated March 10, 2016 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the Register of
  Demands for the City of Cerritos dated March 10, 2016 in the total amount of
  $730,297.00 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of February
  25, 2016 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of February 25, 2016
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Approval of the Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending January 31, 2016
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the
  Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending January 31, 2016 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR
  AGENCY). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for Liberty Park, Jacob
  Park and Bettencourt Park playground equipment and improvements,
  Project No. 10073, Bid No. 1239-16 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works. A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.
 City of Cerritos  March 10, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 5

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $332,431 for Citywide Playground Equipment
  and Improvements, Project No. 10073, Bid No. 1239-16, to WCCR Construction
  and reject the other bid; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related change
  orders; and
  3. Authorize staff to negotiate with WCCR Construction for additional playground
  improvements with available budgeted funds for a total project cost not to exceed
  $372,000 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for installation of playground
  surfacing at Jacob Park, East and West, Project No. 10074, Bid No. 1234-16
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Edwards, to reject all bids and
  authorize staff to re-advertise the project (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of an informational report on the Gateway Cities
  Council of Governments Strategic Transportation Plan (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works. A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed and an additional report was given by
  Robert Campbell, representing the Gateway Cities Council of Governments. A
  document entitled, “Gateway Cities Strategic Transportation Plan” was
  submitted to the City Council for the record.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.
 City of Cerritos  March 10, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 5

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9C.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to receive and file the
  report (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9D.  Review and consideration of award of Bid No. 1235-16 for the supply of 5/8 x
  3/4 inch positive displacement water meters magnetically driven (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Ryan Carey, Budget Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Pulido, to award Bid No. 1235-16 to
  Zenner USA in the amount of $42.52 per unit for a three (3) year term for the annual
  supply of 5/8 x 3/4 inch positive displacement water meters magnetically driven
  (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9E.  Review and consideration of award of Bid No. 1236-16 for the supply and
  installation of three rotary gas meters and related hardware for three engines
  located at 16540 Marquardt Ave., Cerritos, CA (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Ryan Carey, Budget Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Ray, to award Bid No. 1236-16
  to Don Peterson Construction Inc., in the amount of $29,521.56 for the supply and
  installation of three (3) rotary gas meters and related hardware for three (3) engines
  located at 16540 Marquardt Avenue, Cerritos, CA with a one (1) year warranty term
  (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  March 10, 2016

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State
  or Federal Legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards, Pulido and Solanki, Mayor

  CONSENSUS (Chen): Direct the City Manager to include as part of the
  upcoming budget process a report regarding multi-year assessment of
  infrastructure needs, in particular streets and sidewalks.
